Let \(L(g)=d(e,g)\). Since the metric is left-invariant,

\[
d(g,h)=L(g^{-1}h),
\]

so the quadratic form is the convolution form associated to the function \(L^p\).

A direct word-length calculation gives

\[
\#\{g:L(g)=0,1,2,3\}=1,6,16,4.
\]

More explicitly, the only lengths needed below are that \(L\) takes values \(0,1,2,3\). Put

\[
A=2^p,\qquad B=3^p.
\]

The convolution operator with kernel \(L^p\) diagonalizes under the irreducible representations of the Heisenberg group \(H\). There are:

- nine \(1\)-dimensional representations, of which the trivial one corresponds to constants;
- two \(3\)-dimensional representations, each appearing with multiplicity \(3\) in the regular representation.

For the nontrivial \(1\)-dimensional representations, the eigenvalues are

\[
3-2A-2B \quad \text{and} \quad B-2A.
\]

For the \(3\)-dimensional representations, the relevant matrix is

\[
M=
\begin{pmatrix}
1-2A & 1-B & 1-B\\
1-B & -2+A & 1-3A+2B\\
1-B & 1-3A+2B & -2+A
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

One eigenvalue is

\[
-3+4A-2B,
\]

and the remaining two have trace

\[
2B-4A
\]

and determinant

\[
\Delta(p)=4A^2-4AB-2B^2+6B-3.
\]

Thus negative type holds exactly while all these nontrivial eigenvalues are \(\le 0\). The first obstruction is when

\[
\Delta(p)=0,
\]

i.e.

\[
4\cdot 4^p-4\cdot 6^p-2\cdot 9^p+6\cdot 3^p-3=0.
\]

This equation has a unique positive root in \((0,1)\), numerically

\[
\wp \approx 0.4450296403639729.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), exactly one eigenvalue in each of the two \(3\)-dimensional irreducible blocks vanishes. Since each such representation occurs with multiplicity \(3\), the equality space has dimension

\[
2\cdot 3=6.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{(\wp,\dim E)=\left(\rho,6\right)}
\]

where \(\rho\) is the unique positive solution of

\[
\boxed{4\cdot 4^\rho-4\cdot 6^\rho-2\cdot 9^\rho+6\cdot 3^\rho-3=0}
\]

and \(\rho\approx 0.4450296403639729\).
